Question: What is the purpose of the Custom Order Form?
Answer: It is a detailed questionnaire and process guide that makes ordering one-of-a-kind solid hardwood furniture less daunting, especially for first-time customers. It walks you through every decision, sets realistic expectations, and ensures clear communication so the final piece perfectly matches your needs.

Question: What are the most important rules of thumb when ordering custom furniture from Black Barrel Wood Co.?
Answer:
1. Needs vs Wants: Identify non-negotiable needs (e.g., exact dimensions, must-have drawers, specific wood) versus flexible wants (e.g., drawer pulls, secondary wood).
2. Pictures are your best friend: Send as many reference photos as possible — legs from one image, colour from another, hardware from a third.
3. Defer if unsure: Ask for recommendations; the team has tried almost everything and will guide you.
4. Price: Discuss a real budget range early — custom work uses premium materials and craftsmanship and is neither fast, easy, nor cheap, but it’s worth it for a true 1-of-1 piece.
5. Timelines: Take your time in the design phase; changes later are more time-consuming, expensive, and frustrating.

Question: What is the step-by-step process for commissioning a custom piece?
Answer:
1. Initial discussion to outline budget, timeline, needs, and wants; you receive and complete the questionnaire.
2. The team creates a basic design mock-up with measurements, proportions, and visuals.
3. You review and provide one round of changes (free if it leads to an order); updated design sent back for review and sign-off.
4. Once approved, pay 50% deposit and building begins with periodic progress photos.
5. Near completion, pickup or delivery is arranged.

Question: What if I want more than one round of design changes?
Answer: The first round of changes is free (if it leads to an order). Additional rounds after the first cost $150 per round (this fee is credited toward the final cost if you proceed). Changes after final sign-off are more expensive and will delay the project, so it’s best to get it right during the design phase.

Question: Will I see renderings of my piece before building starts?
Answer: Yes. As a free courtesy you receive basic 3D renderings showing the final look, measurements, and proportions — one preliminary after submitting the questionnaire, and a second after your first round of changes (if needed). These help you visualize the piece. High-resolution photorealistic renderings are available for an extra fee.

Question: What furniture styles can Black Barrel Wood Co. build?
Answer: They can build almost any style, including Mid-century, Modern Rustic, Farmhouse, Traditional, Transitional, and styles that are difficult to classify. Send reference images of pieces you like — the more photos, the better.

Question: How do I choose a style if I'm not sure?
Answer: Send reference photos of pieces you like, even if they mix different styles. The team will help synthesize a cohesive look that fits your space and needs.

Question: Which wood species does Black Barrel Wood Co. use and recommend?
Answer:
They primarily use seven locally sourced domestic hardwoods. Foreign/exotic species are possible but usually more costly and sometimes unavailable. Breakdown (price level $ to $$$$):
• Poplar (Light/medium, low density, $) — Straight-grained, great inexpensive secondary wood for drawers, shelves, supports; can be primary too.
• Red Oak (Medium, high density, $) — Extremely strong, great value, open-grained (grain visible and textured even when painted).
• Ash (Light, high density, $$) — Very hard, light-coloured with grain variation, more closed grain than oak.
• Cherry (Medium, medium density, $$$) — Orange to light tan, closed-grain, sands extremely smooth, beautiful grain variation.
• Maple (Very light, very high density, $$$) — Bright white, extremely heavy and dense, sands smooth; great for contrast. Soft maple also available (softer, sometimes streaked).
• Walnut (Dark, medium density, $$$$) — Highly desirable for high-end work, machines beautifully.
• White Oak (Medium/light, very high density, $$$$) — Extremely hard, gorgeous and durable; currently very difficult to source.

Question: How do I choose the right wood species?
Answer: Discuss your priorities (colour, durability, budget, grain visibility) with the team. They will recommend the best match based on your needs.

Question: What are edge profiles and why do they matter?
Answer: The two primary options are round-overs and chamfers. They soften sharp hardwood edges, improve safety and feel, and help prevent dings or splintering. Specified by radius (¼ circle or 45° corner when viewed edge-on). You can choose any radius that fits your design.

Question: What finishes does Black Barrel Wood Co. normally use?
Answer:
Default recommendations (unless you request otherwise):
• Osmo Poly-X hard wax oil — Clear top coat; buildable sheen from matte to semi-gloss; versatile and reliable.
• Rubio Monocoat — Colour-infused, matte-satin finish; excellent protection.

Other finishes (e.g., polyurethane, polycrylic, mineral oil + beeswax for food-safe items) are possible but may offer less durability or add cost. Always discuss your intended use so they can recommend the best protection.

Question: What should I consider when choosing hardware (pulls, slides, hinges, legs)?
Answer: Decide on: Action (push-to-open, soft-close, full-extension, etc.), Finish (stainless, brushed nickel, black, copper, etc.), and Style (modern, traditional, transitional, farmhouse, etc.). Price varies widely.

Question: What custom details or special features can I request?

Question: How long does a custom piece take?

Question: Do you offer pickup and delivery?

Question: How much does a custom piece cost?
